From this viewpoint, the manufacturers plans are not really voluntary once a standard requires them to comply with their plans. In addition, this view recognizes that the voluntary plans were prompted, at least in part, by the knowledge that an average fuel economy standard would be in effect in MY 1979. On the other hand, it can be argued that the only impact brought about by the AFES results from manufacturers' actions to meet the AFES over and above their voluntary plans. From this viewpoint, all other impacts would happen regardless of whether the AFES were established, and are, therefore, not attributable to it.
Both of the viewpoints just discussed have merit.

Therefore, rather than rejecting one in favor of the other, the agency decided to analyze the environmental impact from both points of view.
